identity.title: Machine Learning Engineering
identity.subtitle: From Task Contract to Operating Evidence
identity.author: Komal Nakrani

thesis: Machine learning engineering turns an approved purpose and admissible data into a versioned learning workload whose candidate, qualification evidence, executable identity, operating envelope, recovery path, and retirement record remain inspectable as the system changes.
readerPromise: The reader will be able to contract, construct, qualify, release, observe, diagnose, requalify, and retire a bounded learning workload while keeping adjacent product, domain, evaluation, platform, SRE, security, safety, privacy, governance, legal, and risk-acceptance authority explicit and external.
audience: Production-capable software, data, applied-AI, and ML engineers moving into end-to-end workload accountability
Technical leads who must review workload evidence and technical dispositions
prerequisites: Production programming, tests, APIs, and version control
Ordinary service, deployment, and incident concepts
exitCapability: Produce and hostile-review a complete release, recovery, requalification, control, and retirement dossier for one bounded learning workload without self-authorizing adjacent formal decisions.
exclusions: Beginner programming or generalized data engineering
LLM post-training, prompting, retrieval, or agent-action specialization
Generalized MLOps, platform, fleet-SRE, security, safety, privacy, governance, legal, product, or domain curricula
Framework, provider, model-family, or certification training

parts.title: Bench Zero: Define the Workload
parts.qualificationQuestion: Is there an owned, bounded learning decision with a retained incumbent and explicit authority map?

parts.title: Setup: Make Inputs Admissible
parts.qualificationQuestion: Can every input, label, transformation, split, and serving representation be traced and tested?

parts.title: Fit: Make Changes Reconstructible
parts.qualificationQuestion: Can the candidate comparison be reconstructed without erasing the incumbent or overstating reproducibility?

parts.title: Stress and Qualify: Earn a Disposition
parts.qualificationQuestion: Does the evidence support PASS, HOLD, or REJECT for the named population, segments, and consequences?

parts.title: Bind: Make the Release Inspectable
parts.qualificationQuestion: Can the exact executable, consumer contract, lineage, integrity evidence, and recovery identity travel together?

parts.title: Serve, Watch, Revise: Operate Under Change
parts.qualificationQuestion: Can the workload operate inside a measured envelope and change only through evidence-bearing containment or requalification?

parts.title: Control and Close: Preserve Evidence Through the End
parts.qualificationQuestion: Can accumulated controls, formal decisions, retirement, and non-serving evidence withstand hostile review?

chapters.title: The MLE Decision Center
chapters.decisionJob: Locate the workload-specific MLE decision inside the full lifecycle and authority map.
chapters.thesis: The unit of work is an evidence-bearing learning workload, not a model file, dashboard, or job title.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Distinguish MLE accountability from every adjacent owner and name the evidence state of a workload.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A team treats a trained artifact and an org-chart title as sufficient ownership evidence.
chapters.companionIncrement: Create immutable case index, evidence-state enum, owner registry, and canonical IDs.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port exposes the same decision center, evidence state, and external authority map.
chapters.authorityOwner: Product and domain authorities own purpose; named specialists own formal gates.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE identifies and supplies evidence but does not absorb adjacent authority.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Workload identity, evidence state, and decision rights precede implementation.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Classify an ambiguous request, artifact, owner, and state without using title-based shortcuts.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic lifecycle and authority rail; no ImageGen required.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research sources that distinguish workload ownership from title and tool ownership.

chapters.title: Contract the Task and Decision Rights
chapters.decisionJob: Convert an approved purpose into a bounded task contract with explicit decision owners and a NO-ML or HOLD path.
chapters.thesis: A model cannot be qualified until intended use, excluded use, population, decision, constraints, and authority are reviewable.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Issue a versioned task contract whose missing owner or unjustified ML use fails closed.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A technically feasible model is proposed without an authorized purpose, population, or risk owner.
chapters.companionIncrement: Validate intended and excluded use, population, decision, owner, constraints, and missing-owner failures.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Mechanisms vary; task, population, incumbent, consequence, owner, and exit semantics do not.
chapters.authorityOwner: Product owns purpose and priority; domain and formal authorities own validity and permissibility.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE translates an approved purpose into technical evidence requirements but cannot authorize it.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Purpose, population, non-goals, and decision rights are versioned inputs.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Repair a task contract that lacks an owner, exclusion, or NO-ML branch.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic task-contract airlock and owner matrix.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Find evidence for task contracts, intended use, and preserved authority.

chapters.title: Retain the Incumbent and Name Consequences
chapters.decisionJob: Bind a measurable incumbent, consequence model, segment obligations, and acceptance target before candidate work.
chapters.thesis: A candidate has no meaningful improvement claim without a retained baseline and consequence-aware acceptance contract.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Execute the incumbent and distinguish target, threshold, consequence, and unresolved assumption.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A new model is called better using a metric that was never tied to the incumbent or consequence.
chapters.companionIncrement: Execute deterministic incumbent and acceptance-matrix checks.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port retains a runnable incumbent and the same consequence-linked decision thresholds.
chapters.authorityOwner: Product and domain owners accept the consequence model; evaluation owns independent gate adequacy.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE implements and measures the incumbent but does not set business or domain tolerance alone.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Baseline retention and consequence-linked acceptance precede optimization.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Reject an aggregate improvement that violates a named consequence threshold.
chapters.visualDecision: Selectable baseline-versus-target decision table.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research support for incumbents, consequence matrices, and acceptance criteria.

chapters.title: Make Data and Labels Contractual
chapters.decisionJob: Define admissible dataset and label identities with provenance, access, retention, domain, and exception ownership.
chapters.thesis: Data and labels are executable lifecycle contracts, not anonymous training inputs.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Validate a dataset snapshot and label contract and route every exception to its owner.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A clean schema hides invalid provenance, label meaning, retention, or population use.
chapters.companionIncrement: Validate schema, domains, label semantics, provenance, access, retention, and exception fixtures.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port binds exact input and label identities even when storage and feature mechanisms differ.
chapters.authorityOwner: Data owners retain source truth, access, retention, and shared pipeline authority; domain owners retain label validity.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE owns workload-facing contracts and conformance, not the enterprise data estate or legal basis.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Input and label meaning, provenance, population, and permissions travel with evidence.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Diagnose a fixture whose schema passes but provenance or label meaning is invalid.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic data-contract layers and label lineage table.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research executable data contracts, label definitions, access, and retention boundaries.

chapters.title: Trace Features, Transformations, and Feedback
chapters.decisionJob: Bind feature identity, transformations, feedback arrival, and source/consumer lineage without owning shared data architecture.
chapters.thesis: A feature is supportable only when its computation, upstream truth, downstream consumers, and feedback path remain inspectable.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Trace exact upstream and downstream IDs and detect an undeclared feedback or consumer dependency.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: An individually correct transformation creates hidden skew or feedback through an undeclared consumer.
chapters.companionIncrement: Hash transformation outputs and trace source, feature, consumer, and label-arrival identities.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Each port exposes the same transformation and feedback evidence even when feature computation moves.
chapters.authorityOwner: Data/platform owners retain shared sources and services; consumers own their product behavior.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE specifies and tests workload transformations, not enterprise data-platform topology.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Transformations, consumers, feedback, and source truth need explicit identity.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Find a hidden dependency in a transformation/feedback graph and route its owner.
chapters.visualDecision: Selective ImageGen candidate for a dimensional lineage/feedback cutaway plus selectable companion table.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research system-interface failures, lineage, and feedback dependencies.

chapters.title: Split Without Leakage and Test Train-Serve Conformance
chapters.decisionJob: Choose population-aware splits and prove that training and serving transformations conform.
chapters.thesis: A candidate is inadmissible when time, identity, population, or transformation leakage contaminates its evidence.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Fail a leaked split, stale identity, or serving-transform mismatch and record bounded exceptions.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A high offline result depends on future information or a serving path that computes different inputs.
chapters.companionIncrement: Run temporal, group, population, leakage, identity, and train-serve conformance failures.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports prove equivalent split identity and train-serve semantics despite different execution mechanics.
chapters.authorityOwner: Domain/evaluation owners judge representativeness; platform/data owners retain shared runtime/source authority.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE designs workload splits and conformance tests but cannot self-certify population validity.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Split identity, leakage tests, and train-serve conformance are release evidence.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Repair a temporal/group leak and explain the strongest remaining limitation.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic split rails and train/serve parity matrix.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research primary evidence for splitting, leakage, and conformance.

chapters.title: Build Baselines and Controlled Comparisons
chapters.decisionJob: Design a controlled experiment that retains the incumbent and changes only the claimed intervention.
chapters.thesis: An experiment is useful only when its hypothesis, controls, inputs, and comparison target make the change attributable.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Run a frozen baseline/candidate harness and detect a confounded comparison.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A candidate wins because data, preprocessing, or evaluation changed with the model.
chapters.companionIncrement: Execute baseline and candidate against frozen inputs with a confounding mutation.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port preserves the intervention, control variables, incumbent, and evidence contract.
chapters.authorityOwner: Applied Science owns scientific novelty claims; evaluation retains suite adequacy.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE owns workload experiment integrity, not the research agenda or independent gate.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Retained baselines and controlled variables make candidate evidence attributable.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Identify and repair a comparison whose apparent gain is confounded.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic experiment card and changed-variable ledger.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research primary sources for controlled ML experiments and baselines.

chapters.title: Bind Run Identity and Bounded Reproducibility
chapters.decisionJob: Freeze code, data, dependency, parameter, seed, hardware, and execution-context identity and state the strongest supportable rerun claim.
chapters.thesis: Reproducibility is a bounded evidence statement, not a universal bit-for-bit promise.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Validate a run manifest and explain a deliberate cross-context divergence without erasing it.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A same-seed rerun diverges across hardware and the team upgrades local repeatability into an absolute claim.
chapters.companionIncrement: Validate manifests/hashes and record a deliberate cross-context divergence fixture.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports record comparable identities and context limits; none promises universal bit determinism.
chapters.authorityOwner: Platform owners define supported runtime; research/evaluation owners retain claim-validity decisions.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE records and tests bounded reconstruction, not universal determinism.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Immutable run identity and honest context limits make evidence reconstructible.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Write the strongest defensible reproducibility statement from two divergent runs.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic run capsule and bounded-divergence comparison.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research bounded reproducibility and required run identities.

chapters.title: Compare Candidates Without Losing the Baseline
chapters.decisionJob: Select a candidate for qualification while retaining baseline, failed candidates, limitations, and evidence lineage.
chapters.thesis: Candidate selection is an evidence-routing decision, not a release pass or a deletion of losing evidence.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Produce a limitation-bearing candidate-for-qualification record and retain the incumbent.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: Selection erases a failed segment, failed candidate, or baseline and is mistaken for qualification.
chapters.companionIncrement: Produce deterministic candidate comparison with explicit limitations and retained baseline.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Selection consumes the same comparison evidence and never implies release authority.
chapters.authorityOwner: Evaluation retains qualification validity; Applied Science retains scientific-claim authority.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE nominates a candidate but cannot self-certify the independent gate.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Candidate identity retains baselines, failures, limitations, and comparison lineage.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Refuse a candidate record that omits its failed segment or incumbent.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic candidate ledger with retained baseline rail.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research candidate comparison without release overclaim.

chapters.title: Represent Populations and Consequential Segments
chapters.decisionJob: Build a representative suite and segment gate whose thresholds follow consequence rather than aggregate convenience.
chapters.thesis: Aggregate performance cannot authorize a candidate when consequential populations or segments fail.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Calculate exact segment results and enforce consequence-linked precedence over the mean.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: The average improves while a protected or high-consequence segment regresses.
chapters.companionIncrement: Calculate exact aggregate/segment metrics and enforce gate precedence.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port uses the same named population, segment, consequence, and precedence contract.
chapters.authorityOwner: Evaluation owns suite adequacy; product/domain/formal authorities own acceptable consequences.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE implements, diagnoses, and remediates but cannot waive a consequential gate.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Representative populations and consequence-linked segments outrank aggregate convenience.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Issue HOLD when aggregate gain conflicts with a critical segment threshold.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic segment matrix and threshold plot; no raster numeric truth.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research primary sources for population and segment qualification.

chapters.title: Treat Uncertainty, Calibration, and Failure as Evidence
chapters.decisionJob: Record uncertainty or calibration where applicable, sample limits, error taxonomy, and unresolved evidence.
chapters.thesis: A score becomes decision evidence only when its uncertainty, calibration relevance, failure families, and limitations are explicit.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Interpret calibration and resampling evidence without converting it into universal confidence.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A well-calibrated aggregate hides sparse evidence, an important error family, or an inapplicable probability interpretation.
chapters.companionIncrement: Run exact calibration/resampling fixtures and mutation tests for missing limits.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports expose uncertainty, failure, and limitation evidence appropriate to their model output.
chapters.authorityOwner: Evaluation owns method adequacy; domain/safety authorities judge consequential error sufficiency.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE computes and diagnoses evidence but cannot turn method output into formal acceptance.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Uncertainty, calibration applicability, failure taxonomy, and sample limits travel with metrics.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Repair an overconfident qualification note using sample and failure evidence.
chapters.visualDecision: Selectable reliability strip, interval table, and failure taxonomy.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research primary sources for calibration, uncertainty, and error taxonomies.

chapters.title: Issue a Technical Qualification Disposition
chapters.decisionJob: Combine population, segment, uncertainty, consequence, limitation, owner, and rollback evidence into PASS, HOLD, or REJECT.
chapters.thesis: Technical qualification is an explicit disposition with authority boundaries, not a single score or self-approved launch.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Issue a complete disposition that blocks incomplete or self-authorized evidence.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A technically strong candidate self-certifies evaluation or ignores a missing formal owner.
chapters.companionIncrement: Gate engine rejects self-authorization, missing evidence, and illegal progress from HOLD or REJECT.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports produce the same disposition fields and authority separation.
chapters.authorityOwner: Independent evaluation and relevant formal authorities retain stop-ship and acceptance decisions.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE issues the workload technical disposition and routes external decisions; it cannot self-approve them.
chapters.durableDoctrine: PASS, HOLD, and REJECT bind evidence, population, owner, limitation, rollback, and next evidence.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Produce a HOLD or REJECT record that names repair and requalification rather than hiding failure.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic Qualification Gate page and decision table.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research technical disposition and independent gate evidence.

chapters.title: Release a Package Plus Evidence
chapters.decisionJob: Bind executable artifact, dependencies, interface, intended/excluded use, evaluated bounds, approvals, limitations, hashes, and previous-good target.
chapters.thesis: A release is the exact executable plus the evidence required to understand, operate, and recover it.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Build a release manifest whose every evidence link resolves and whose approval boundaries remain explicit.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A registry entry points to an artifact but loses evaluated bounds, limitations, or recovery identity.
chapters.companionIncrement: Build release manifest and verify artifact, dependency, interface, approval, limit, and recovery links.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port accepts the same release evidence schema even when package mechanics differ.
chapters.authorityOwner: Security, platform, product, domain, and evaluation owners retain their formal approvals.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE assembles and verifies the workload package but cannot fabricate or substitute approvals.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Executable identity and supporting evidence are one releasable unit.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Reject a package whose executable hash resolves but evaluated bounds or recovery target do not.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic release manifest and optional package cutaway only if dimensionality helps.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research release bundles, evidence records, and recovery identity.

chapters.title: Bind Interfaces, Consumers, and Compatibility
chapters.decisionJob: Freeze request/response contracts, consumer identities, coexistence/migration evidence, and fallback ownership.
chapters.thesis: A model release is unsafe when its consumers, interfaces, compatibility window, or fallback owner are implicit.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Run old/new consumer fixtures and produce a controlled compatibility or migration disposition.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: An undeclared consumer or incompatible response shape turns a valid model into a failing product path.
chapters.companionIncrement: Run contract, backward-compatibility, coexistence, migration, and fallback-owner tests.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports expose equivalent interface, consumer, migration, and fallback evidence.
chapters.authorityOwner: Consumer/application owners accept product compatibility; platform owners own shared interface support.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE validates workload compatibility but does not own every consuming application or agent effect.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Interfaces, consumers, coexistence, migration, and fallback are versioned release evidence.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Diagnose a migration that passes the new client but strands an undeclared old consumer.
chapters.visualDecision: Selective ImageGen candidate for release-consumer dependency cutaway plus selectable contract table.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research compatibility, consumer registries, and migration evidence.

chapters.title: Preserve Integrity, Lineage, and Recovery Identity
chapters.decisionJob: Verify end-to-end lineage, inventory, integrity, access evidence, promotion packet, and previous-good recovery identity.
chapters.thesis: A releasable workload must prove what it is, where it came from, who may use it, and what exact state can replace it.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Fail tampered, unsigned, unauthorized, or unrecoverable package mutations.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: The candidate is valid but its dependency, signer, access, lineage, or previous-good identity is ambiguous.
chapters.companionIncrement: Mutate hashes, lineage, signer, access, inventory, and recovery identities and fail closed.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports preserve verifiable lineage, integrity, access, and previous-good identity.
chapters.authorityOwner: Security owns control requirements and exceptions; platform owners own shared promotion mechanisms.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE implements/tests workload controls and supplies evidence without self-approving security exceptions.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Integrity, lineage, inventory, access, and recovery identity are continuous release controls.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Trace and reject a package with correct metrics but a broken integrity or recovery chain.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic integrity chain and recovery identity table.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research integrity, lineage, inventory, access, and recovery controls.

chapters.title: Measure the Serving Envelope
chapters.decisionJob: Measure representative demand, latency, error, capacity, staged exposure, bake/abort rules, and degraded mode for the workload.
chapters.thesis: Serving readiness is a bounded operating envelope, not an unqualified benchmark or deployment event.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Issue a staged operating disposition from deterministic request traces without claiming fleet or production performance.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: An average latency benchmark hides tail failure, resource saturation, or an absent degraded mode.
chapters.companionIncrement: Replay synthetic request traces and assert envelope, staged exposure, bake, abort, and degraded-mode records.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports report comparable demand, latency, error, capacity, failure, and limitation evidence.
chapters.authorityOwner: Platform/SRE own fleet capacity, SLOs, and incident command; product owns exposure intent.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE owns model-workload envelope evidence, not generalized fleet reliability.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Representative operating envelopes bind demand, tail behavior, failure, capacity, and rollback.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Reject a serving claim that uses only mean latency or extrapolates beyond its fixture.
chapters.visualDecision: Selectable latency/capacity plots; selective ImageGen cutaway for failure propagation only.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research serving-envelope and staged-exposure evidence.

chapters.title: Observe Without Inventing Ground Truth
chapters.decisionJob: Bind observation signals, delayed labels, proxies, drift, segments, owners, and alert-to-decision routes without automatic truth claims.
chapters.thesis: Monitoring is evidence routing under incomplete truth, not a dashboard that authorizes retraining or promotion.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Replay an observation stream, preserve label delay and uncertainty, and route alerts without inventing outcomes.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A proxy drift alert is treated as ground truth and triggers an unreviewed retrain or promotion.
chapters.companionIncrement: Replay fixed observation stream; preserve delayed outcomes; block auto-retrain and auto-promote.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port exposes truth availability, proxy limits, segments, owners, and decision routes.
chapters.authorityOwner: Evaluation/domain owners define sufficient evidence; SRE/platform own shared telemetry and incident mechanisms.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE diagnoses workload evidence but cannot invent ground truth or automate formal disposition.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Signals, truth delay, proxy limits, drift, owners, and actions are explicit contracts.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Convert a drift alert into an investigation record without claiming outcome degradation.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic signal lattice, label-delay rail, and alert-to-decision map.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research observation under delayed ground truth and drift limits.

chapters.title: Contain, Roll Back, Repair, and Requalify
chapters.decisionJob: Separate incident command from workload diagnosis, contain or roll back, bind changed evidence, and require a new candidate identity after repair.
chapters.thesis: A model incident closes only when containment, evidence change, recovery identity, and requalification are explicit.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Replay an incident and produce containment/rollback plus a new evidence-bearing candidate or a durable hold.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A retrained artifact silently replaces the release without a new identity, changed-evidence diff, or independent requalification.
chapters.companionIncrement: Replay incident state machine; require command/decision split, containment, changed-evidence diff, new candidate, and requalification.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports preserve incident authority, containment, changed evidence, recovery, and requalification semantics.
chapters.authorityOwner: SRE owns incident command/fleet action; evaluation and formal authorities retain their gates.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE owns model-specific diagnosis and repair evidence, not fleet command or risk acceptance.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Containment, rollback, repair, and requalification preserve identity and authority under change.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Reject a same-identity retrain and build a valid changed-evidence requalification packet.
chapters.visualDecision: Selective ImageGen candidate for incident/requalification chain plus semantic state table.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research model-specific incident, rollback, repair, and requalification evidence.

chapters.title: Trace Controls, Exceptions, and Formal Decisions
chapters.decisionJob: Integrate workload-specific control tests, exceptions, residual limits, and formal decisions accumulated since the task contract.
chapters.thesis: Controls and authority are continuous fields in every dossier delta; this chapter tests their trace rather than introducing a late checklist.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Prove that every control, exception, residual limit, owner, and formal decision has a valid history and no self-approval.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A final checklist masks missing earlier evidence, an unsigned exception, or an authority that never approved the decision.
chapters.companionIncrement: Run least-privilege, integrity, exception, owner, residual-limit, and unsigned/unapproved mutation checks.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: All ports preserve the same control evidence and external authority while implementation mechanics vary.
chapters.authorityOwner: Security, safety, privacy, governance, legal, product, domain, and evaluation owners retain formal decisions.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE implements/tests workload controls and routes exceptions but cannot self-approve them.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Control evidence and formal authority are threaded through the lifecycle, not bolted on at release.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Trace an exception backward and fail it if its evidence or authority is absent.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic control-evidence chain; optional trust cutaway only if it improves relationship comprehension.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research continuous control evidence and formal-decision traceability.

chapters.title: Retire the Workload and Prove Non-Serving State
chapters.decisionJob: Execute retirement across consumers, endpoints, credentials, monitoring, registry, retention, recovery, and archive, then prove no serving path remains.
chapters.thesis: Retirement is a verifiable terminal workload state, not a delete button or a stale registry label.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Produce verified non-serving evidence while preserving required retention and recovery records.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: The endpoint is deleted while credentials, consumers, monitoring, fallback routes, or registry aliases can still serve the model.
chapters.companionIncrement: Decommission fixture state only and audit consumers, endpoints, credentials, monitors, registry aliases, retention, and recovery.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: Every port proves non-serving state across its own paths using the same terminal evidence semantics.
chapters.authorityOwner: Product/domain/formal authorities approve retirement and retention; platform/security owners execute shared shutdown controls.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE verifies workload non-serving evidence but cannot set legal retention or shared-system policy.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Retirement requires consumer, endpoint, credential, monitoring, registry, retention, and recovery proof.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Find a residual serving path after nominal deletion and repair the retirement record.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic non-serving proof matrix; optional retirement cutaway paired with Chapter 19 only if useful.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research evidence-preserving retirement and non-serving verification.

chapters.title: Review the Dossier and Raise the Standard
chapters.decisionJob: Hostile-review the complete dossier, derive one reusable workload standard, and route one systemic issue to its actual owner.
chapters.thesis: Advanced MLE practice raises evidence quality through artifact review and routed system improvement, not title, novelty, or generic leadership advice.
chapters.readerEndpoint: Validate the complete release/recovery/retirement chain and propose a reusable standard without taking another team's authority.
chapters.uniqueFailurePressure: A senior review becomes career advice, a tool checklist, or an MLE-owned platform policy instead of evidence-based improvement.
chapters.companionIncrement: One offline verify-dossier entry point checks identities, links, authority records, five ports, and terminal non-serving state.
chapters.fivePortInvariant: The reusable standard is expressed through the shared interface and passes all five ports without privileged depth.
chapters.authorityOwner: Each specialist retains its decision; organization owners decide shared platform or policy adoption.
chapters.mleCeiling: The MLE mentors through evidence review and routes systemic issues; it does not unilaterally set cross-team policy.
chapters.durableDoctrine: Advanced scope is wider evidence radius, ambiguity, initiative, mentoring, and standards—not novelty or title.
chapters.assessmentEvidence: Hostile-review the full dossier, identify one local defect and one systemic issue, and route both correctly.
chapters.visualDecision: Semantic portfolio evidence map and closing dossier; no decorative climax.
chapters.phase06Handoff: Research advanced scope and evidence-standard practices without career-advice drift.

nonDuplication.name: Accountability-center test
nonDuplication.definition: state its primary engineering decision in one sentence. Fail if that decision is already the accountable center of `PUB-01` through `PUB-05`.

nonDuplication.name: Reader-endpoint test
nonDuplication.definition: name a demonstrable before/after capability. Fail if completing an existing publication already produces the same endpoint without a new workload-qualification obligation.

nonDuplication.name: Unit-of-work test
nonDuplication.definition: the durable output must be a versioned learning workload and qualification dossier. Fail if it is principally a customer engagement, AI application experience, acting agent, language behavior system, or LLM adaptation program.

nonDuplication.name: Artifact-spine test
nonDuplication.definition: map each proposed artifact to a new MLE disposition. Fail if the artifact chain merely renames an existing book's capstone artifacts or repeats them in the same dependency order.

nonDuplication.name: Replaceability test
nonDuplication.definition: replace any LLM, agentic, customer, or generative-AI example with a classical, statistical, deep-learning, or physical/edge workload. Fail if the teaching objective collapses.

nonDuplication.name: Specialist-depth test
nonDuplication.definition: apply `BND-01` through `BND-17`. Fail if supporting knowledge becomes the adjacent profession's generalized curriculum or authority.

nonDuplication.name: Prose-and-architecture originality test
nonDuplication.definition: compare proposed text, case premises, figures, tables, and content progression against all five publications. Fail on copied/paraphrased prose, distinctive case reuse, or inherited chapter/part architecture; a shared industry term is not by itself duplication.

nonDuplication.name: Evidence-newness test
nonDuplication.definition: require MLE claim IDs, workload-specific decisions, and current sources for every substantive claim. Fail if an existing publication is treated as the technical source or evidence base.

nonDuplication.name: Outcome-not-topic test
nonDuplication.definition: overlap in a topic such as evaluation, deployment, monitoring, security, or change passes only when the owner, evidence, and disposition differ. Fail if the difference is merely a title change.

nonDuplication.name: Merge-or-route test
nonDuplication.definition: remove or route any unit that fails one of the tests above. Do not preserve it for symmetry, marketing coverage, or page count.

creativePolicies.name: Decision job
creativePolicies.definition: every non-prose element names one learning problem and the decision it helps the reader make. Remove it if neither can be stated precisely.
creativePolicies.productionPolicy: Every chapter visualDecision names its decision job.

creativePolicies.name: Evidence trace
creativePolicies.definition: every gate or lab connects input identity, measured evidence, limitation, owner, disposition, and next action. Never present a score, dashboard, registry entry, or model card as complete assurance.
creativePolicies.productionPolicy: Every milestone and gate binds evidence, limitation, owner, disposition, and next evidence.

creativePolicies.name: Semantic color
creativePolicies.definition: use Instrument Blue for baseline/measured evidence, Calibration Lime only for a visibly labeled passed threshold, Diagnostic Rose for a labeled regression/invalidation/intervention/rollback, and Grid Steel for inactive structure. Color is never the only signal.
creativePolicies.productionPolicy: visualSystem palette semantics require labels in addition to color.

creativePolicies.name: Screen-first legibility
creativePolicies.definition: use 7 by 10 portrait pages; Archivo SemiCondensed for orientation, Source Sans 3 at no less than 11.5pt and roughly 1.48 leading for sustained reading, and IBM Plex Mono only for exact technical identities. Captions, tables, code, and footnotes must remain tablet-readable without zoom-dependent microtype.
creativePolicies.productionPolicy: identity geometry and visualSystem fonts enforce 7 by 10 screen-first legibility.

creativePolicies.name: Callout discipline
creativePolicies.definition: callouts must carry a limitation, diagnostic, authority boundary, evidence status, or actionable decision. Decorative quotations, generic motivation boxes, and repeated summaries fail.
creativePolicies.productionPolicy: Learning-pack and visual decisions permit only limitation, diagnostic, authority, evidence, or action callouts.

creativePolicies.name: Lab truth
creativePolicies.definition: a lab identifies whether its result is executed, recorded, illustrative, or synthetic; binds inputs and expected evidence; and never implies production, safety, or business performance it did not observe.
creativePolicies.productionPolicy: Every chapter learning contract and later lab must label executed, recorded, illustrative, or synthetic truth.

creativePolicies.name: Quantitative precision
creativePolicies.definition: exact plots, tables, axes, thresholds, identifiers, and overlays use semantic HTML/CSS so text remains selectable and exact. Raster art must not carry paragraphs or irreplaceable numeric truth.

conventions.crossReferences: Use canonical IDs plus title on first use; later references use the ID. A range abbreviation never changes the exact IDs. Markdown links target stable relative paths and anchors; JSON uses exact IDs.
conventions.artifactIdentity: Every artifact carries stable ID, schema version, artifact version, source/parent identities, content hash, evidence state, owner, authority record, limitations, and supersedes/supersededBy links where applicable.
conventions.supersession: Supersession never deletes prior evidence. A new artifact names the old identity, reason, changed evidence, invalidated claims, new owner decision, and legal reopen state.
conventions.versions: Architecture and schemas use semantic versions. Dossier artifacts use immutable content versions. Edition changes use edition identity and date. Volatile examples record as-of date and source without silently changing durable doctrine.
conventions.phase06Binding: Every Phase 06 source, book claim, case, and chapter research pack references canonical chapter/domain/cluster/claim/boundary/scenario/case IDs and the architecture version/hash consumed.
conventions.companionBinding: Companion commands and expected records use the same IDs, versions, hashes, evidence states, authority fields, and supersession semantics; filenames and provider APIs are never canonical concept identities.

companion.boundary: Offline, provider-neutral, deterministic over fixed synthetic fixtures, pinned dependencies, stable IDs/hashes, no credentials, network, paid service, or real external effect; nondeterminism is measured and recorded rather than denied.
